title: Effect of Resistance Training Frequency on Gains in Muscular Strength: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
population: 22 studies, most in untrained participants; subgroups for young and older adults, men and women.
key_findings: Strength gains grew with weekly frequency: effect sizes of about 0.74, 0.82, 0.93 and 1.08 for training 1, 2, 3 and 4 or more times a week.
With volume equated, frequency had no significant effect on strength, so the authors attribute the overall effect mainly to the extra volume higher frequencies allow.
Subgroups suggested more benefit from higher frequency for multi-joint and upper-body lifts, in women and in young adults.
methods: Systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of studies comparing training frequencies, with subgroup analyses by volume, exercise, body region, failure, age and sex; study quality rated with a modified Downs and Black checklist.
limitations: Only 4 of 22 studies rated good quality, the rest moderate; most participants were untrained, and the authors call for more studies in trained people.

verification.retraction_check: No retraction or correction notice in Crossref updated-by or in the PubMed publication types on 2026-11-25.
